chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) initiated me one day without my asking him, so he said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Every intoxicant is prohibited.' I said, 'May Allah keep you well! Is all of it prohibited?' So he said: 'Yes, even one gulp from it is prohibited.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming even a small amount of an intoxicant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the comprehensive prohibition of all intoxicants, tracing the ruling back to the Prophet Muhammad (saww) through Imam al-Sadiq (as). It clarifies that the prohibition is not limited to large quantities but extends to even a single gulp (jur'ah), establishing a strict standard for consumption. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the permissibility of substances based on their intoxicating properties.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> initiated me one day from without me having asked him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Every intoxicant is Prohibited’. I said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! All of it is Prohibited?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, (even) one dosage from it is prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following:

“One day abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, initiating from himself and without my asking said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, all intoxicating liquor is unlawful.’ I then asked saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, is all of it unlawful?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, even one sip is unlawful.’”
